title: deployment hardening for Render / Cloudflare
trigger: owner intends to host on Render or Cloudflare; asked for quality tested against that target

fixed.defect: the hand-rolled redirect loop rebuilt req_headers from the ORIGINAL headers on every hop, so caller credentials (Tavily Authorization, Brave X-Subscription-Token, Cookie) were forwarded across cross-origin redirects
fixed.note: a helper-level test passed while the real bug persisted; only an end-to-end respx two-hop test exposed it, because the loop body overwrote the stripped headers
fixed.fix: hop_headers thread: narrowed via _strip_credentials on any origin change, and the loop body rebuilds from hop_headers not from headers
fixed.gate1: CAUGHT - end-to-end test fails with 'Authorization leaked across origins' when the strip is disabled

fixed.defect: API keys carried in a URL query string (Stack Exchange uses ?key=) were persisted into cache metadata and interpolated into FetchError text
fixed.fix: redact_url() applied to final_url in cache meta, response object, and error messages; 10 secret parameter names covered case-insensitively

fixed.severity: LOW (availability, but pushed users toward disabling protection)
fixed.defect: MCP matches Host exactly or against host:*; the default entries had no port form, so a real client sending Host: 127.0.0.1:8765 got 421. The documented workaround '*' disables DNS-rebinding protection entirely.
fixed.fix: each configured host is expanded to also allow any port; protection stays ON

fixed.defect: http_port defaulted to 8765 and never read $PORT, so on Render/Cloud Run/Heroku (which inject PORT and route only to it) the server bound the wrong port and every health check failed
fixed.fix: http_port uses AliasChoices('WEBLENS_HTTP_PORT','PORT'); the prefixed name still wins

deployment_verification.method: local process simulated exactly like a platform: PORT injected, no --port flag, bind 0.0.0.0, token from env

not_verified: no real Render deploy was performed (no account access, and the owner has not authorised it)
no Cloudflare deployment was performed; the worker wraps a Durable Object container and was not exercised
Docker image was not built in this environment
no load test against the deployed endpoint
Cloudflare Containers require a paid plan and a container-backed Durable Object; that path is untested here
